title: How to Write Speaker Notes That Become a Great Voiceover (blog explainer)

brief.story: A clear explainer of the post.

slides.title: Speaker Notes That Become a Great Voiceover
bullets: From rough notes to a clear script
slides.notes: Your speaker notes are written for you, not for a listener. Here's how to turn rough notes into a voiceover that sounds clear and natural.

slides.title: Notes Are Fragments, Scripts Are Sentences
bullets: Script: 'Let's look at the results. We tested three groups.'
Tells the viewer where to look
slides.notes: Rough notes work on stage, but a voice needs full sentences. A real script tells the viewer where to look and links smoothly to the next slide.

slides.title: Write the Way You Speak
slides.notes: Read your draft aloud. If you wouldn't say it in conversation, rewrite it. Keep sentences short, because a listener can't scan back up the page.

slides.title: Spell Out What the Voice Trips On
bullets: 3.5% → three and a half per cent
n=240 → two hundred and forty participants
slides.notes: Abbreviations, symbols and numbers can come out oddly. Write them in your notes exactly the way you want them heard.

slides.title: Use Punctuation to Shape the Pace
slides.notes: Narration takes its cues from punctuation. Put an important phrase in its own short sentence, and the listener gets time to absorb each point.

slides.title: Read It Aloud, Then Make the Video
bullets: Full, short sentences in every note
slides.notes: Your polished notes become the narration. On Pro, a.i. directs the video, timing each scene to your words. Try Basic first at powerpoint2vid.com.
